clue.text: Exhausted by pleasure-seeking soon enough

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for worn out, exhausted
someone pleasure-seeking is out for a good time

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out from too much partying, and it served them right before long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, at the proper moment, which is to say soon enough.

clue.text: Firm owned by fool falling for financial opportunism

indicators.note: owned by means held by, so the fool contains the firm word

parts.note: an ass is a fool
firm as in set solid, like a jelly
tripping is stumbling or falling

explanation.surface: A company run by an idiot stumbles in its search for quick profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' tempts as a company; it means SET, which the fool holds: AS-SET-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-stripping is buying a firm cheaply to sell off its assets for profit, a byword for financial opportunism.

clue.text: One game or another held a couple of times

indicators.note: held means contained, so the card game holds the pair of letters

parts.note: another game: loo is an old card game
T is the abbreviation for time, so two times give two Ts

explanation.surface: One game or another was played twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' links the definition to the wordplay; 'another' means another game, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance in which numbers are drawn, a form of lottery.

clue.text: PM and Queen agree to put up with a country

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen
OK means agree, as a verb

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister and the monarch agree to tolerate a rogue state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like tolerate, but 'put up' reverses EROK into KORE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is the country on the northern half of the Korean peninsula.

clue.text: In view of house number over step

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process

explanation.surface: A house number is displayed above a doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a theatre's audience, so in view of the house means on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on stage puts a performer in full sight of the theatre audience.

clue.text: Mogul capital visible in faded picture

indicators.note: visible in means seen within, so the city sits inside the other word

parts.note: faded light is dim
Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, was a capital of the Mughal empire

explanation.surface: An old Mughal capital appears in a faded photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawn picture or plan showing how something works.

clue.text: I back villain in play

parts.note: back as in years back, which means ago

explanation.surface: I support the villain of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal or support; it means AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Fashion centres, at intervals

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape or make, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Fashion hubs, at times.
explanation.definitionFit: Entr'actes are the intervals between acts of a play, or music performed in them.

clue.text: You or I, very involved in criteria clubs set out

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
set out means laid out in order, arranging the letters afresh

explanation.surface: You or I get deeply caught up in arranging the rules for clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges CRITERIA CLUBS and 'involved in' puts V among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruciverbalist is a crossword enthusiast, which is what the solver reading this clue is.

clue.text: Curse about stocking one instrument!

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so the curse word holds the numeral inside it
about signals that the whole result is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Rats! is a mild curse or exclamation of annoyance
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone swears at one musical instrument, exasperated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' puts I inside RATS to give RATIS, and 'about' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument from India.

clue.text: Butcher hoots behind slowcoach in the van

indicators.note: behind places the laughter after the front letter
in the van means at the front, so only the leading letter of slowcoach is taken

parts.note: hoots of mirth are laughter

explanation.surface: A butcher laughs at a slow driver stuck in his delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' tempts as a vehicle; here 'in the van' means at the front, so it picks S from slowcoach.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to slaughter them, kill brutally in numbers; both words are verbs.

clue.text: Visitor leaving kids money for toy hat I supply

indicators.note: read as supply-ly, meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A visitor leaves the children cash to buy a toy hat that she provides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the verb; it is the adverb from supple (pronounced sup-lee), signalling the letters of 'for toy hat I' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The tooth fairy is the nursery figure who swaps a child's lost milk tooth for a coin under the pillow.

clue.text: Secular official, semi-retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the half-word is read backwards
semi means half, here the back half of the word official

explanation.surface: A church officer, now working part-time, has turned to worldly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-retired' takes the back half of OFFICIAL, CIAL, and reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means of the laity rather than the clergy, hence lay or secular.

clue.text: Pudding of a chap, say, upset after he is chucked by woman

indicators.note: after puts the chap and the reversed example behind the shortened name
chucked means dumped, so these letters are thrown out of the woman's name

parts.note: Blanche is a woman's name
taken as written
a man is a chap

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so reversed

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A dessert made of a man upset after his woman dumps him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is chucked by' drops HE from BLANCHE to leave BLANC; 'upset' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blancmange is a set milk pudding, sweet and wobbly, thickened with cornflour.

clue.text: Union upset about end of quotas for silk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the union and the grievance enclose the last letter

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
upset means sore, aggrieved

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of quotas

explanation.surface: A trade union is angry about quota limits on silk imports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but means SORE; the two words TU and SORE go about S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse brownish silk from wild silkworms, also spelt tussah.

clue.text: Second small note half-heartedly offered as bribe

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: the heart of the note is its doubled middle letter, and half of it goes

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A second little banknote is offered without conviction as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: TENNER has NN at its heart; 'half-heartedly' removes one N to give TENER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement offered to win someone over, a euphemism for a bribe.

clue.text: Statesman's change of position almost restricting old group

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the shortened word encloses the rest
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a move is a change of position
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A politician's shift of stance nearly confines an old faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MOVE to MOV, which then wraps OLOT: M-OLOT-OV. The 's after Statesman is a link for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vyacheslav Molotov was the Soviet foreign minister under Stalin, a statesman of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Losing wings, sick bird repelled main danger

indicators.note: wings are the outer letters, so losing them keeps only the inside of sick
repelled means driven back, so the bird is written backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: An ailing bird, its wings failing, fends off a threat from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing wings' leaves IC from sick; 'repelled' turns GREBE into EBERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Main is an old word for the open sea, and an iceberg is the great hazard to shipping there.

clue.text: Soldier Prince, not a leading librettist

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the leading letter is an A, and not means it is dropped

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort

explanation.surface: A soldier prince is not a man of the front rank.
explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A librettist writes the words of an opera; Gilbert wrote them for Sullivan's music.

clue.text: Bust on nurse who doesn't take drugs

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, standing for the noun

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A nurse is caught in a drugs raid but turns out to be clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' suggests a drugs raid; it is the anagram signal for ON NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-user is a person who abstains, here from drugs.

clue.text: Permit found under brass ornament

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the permit below the cheek

parts.note: brass and neck both mean cheek, impudence
let means permit

explanation.surface: A licence is found beneath a brass ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like the metal; it means cheek, NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is an ornament worn around the neck, such as a short necklace.

clue.text: Crown of pear-tree, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: The top of a pear tree is a strange thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the head, especially its top or crown.

clue.text: Van with criminals by filthy road sign, reversing

parts.note: something filthy is black with dirt

indicators.note: reversing turns the road and the sign round together

parts.note: AI stands for the A1, Britain's longest numbered road
the ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Criminals in a van drive past a grimy road sign backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns AIRAM into MARIA. The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: A Black Maria is an old slang name for a police van carrying prisoners.

clue.text: Port container, not right for wine

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: not right means the R, for right, is dropped

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A port container that doesn't suit wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of Spain.

clue.text: After rising go out to lunch

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the attempt is reversed

parts.note: a go or a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: Once up, head out for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' looks like going for a meal; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both bats and out to lunch are slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Chap carrying on, normal or unique?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the name encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Neil is a man's name, a chap
taken as written
par is the normal standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: A man keeps going on, wondering whether he is ordinary or one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' looks like a phrase for continuing; split it, so 'carrying' holds ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is something without equal; the word is used adjectivally to mean unrivalled or unique.

clue.text: Country, one home to old woman

indicators.note: home to means housing, so the country takes in the letter for old

parts.note: Nam is a slang shortening of Vietnam
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A country that is home to an old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The O sits inside NAM, before the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: I bet hesitator is prepared to do what someone else intends

indicators.note: prepared means made up or arranged, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A gambler bets that a dithering person is ready to act on another's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise to the bait is to be provoked into reacting just as someone else hoped.
